2607.05956.title: Integrating knowledge graphs and multilingual scholarly corpora for domain-adaptive LLMs in SSH
2607.05956.paper_summary: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into scientific research workflows, particularly for bibliographic discovery and literature synthesis, raises significant methodological, epistemic and regulatory challenges for the Social Sciences and Humanities (SSH), especially with regard to disciplinary diversity, multilingual access to sources and the evaluation of results. This paper presents an on-going use case developed within the European project LLMs4EU and the ALT-EDIC infrastructure, aimed at adapting foundation models to SSH research practices and supporting tasks such as question answering, comparative document analysis and literature review. The evaluation framework follows the LLMs4EU protocol and encompasses both independent quantitative benchmarking (retrieval, summarisation, traceability and hallucination detection) and a qualitative assessment involving a panel of Digital Humanities experts. By embedding model adaptation within research infrastructures and a structured legal and ethical compliance framework, the use case explores how domain-sensitive and regulation-aware generative AI can support SSH scholarship while preserving reliability and epistemic responsibility.
2607.05956.paper_summary_zh: 將大型語言模型（LLMs）整合進科學研究工作流程，特別是在文獻發現和文獻綜述方面，對社會科學和人文學科（SSH）提出了重大的方法論、認識論和監管挑戰，尤其是在學科多樣性、多語言獲取資料以及結果評估方面。本文介紹了一個在歐洲項目LLMs4EU和ALT-EDIC基礎設施中開發的持續使用案例，旨在將基礎模型調整為適應SSH研究實踐，並支持如問題回答、比較文檔分析和文獻回顧等任務。評估框架遵循LLMs4EU協議，涵蓋獨立的定量基準測試（檢索、摘要、可追溯性和幻覺檢測）以及涉及數位人文專家的質性評估。通過將模型調整嵌入研究基礎設施和結構化的法律與倫理合規框架，這個使用案例探討了如何利用對領域敏感和遵循規範的生成式AI來支持SSH學術研究，同時保持可靠性和認識責任。
